# Answers: What Node is

## Before you start
1. A runtime: it runs JavaScript with the V8 engine and adds its own modules. Source: [Introduction to Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/getting-started/introduction-to-nodejs)
2. Read and write files, open network sockets and start processes. Source: [Introduction to Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/getting-started/introduction-to-nodejs)

## Retrieval practice
1. A runtime around V8 with built-in modules for files, networking and processes, so the language can reach the machine. Source: [Core idea](#core-idea)
2. The browser sandboxes scripts away from the machine; Node exposes it through modules such as fs. Source: [Introduction to Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/getting-started/introduction-to-nodejs)
3. Node loads the file and executes it top to bottom, then keeps running while work is pending. Source: [Core idea](#core-idea)
4. They ship with the runtime and are imported by name, such as `node:fs`. Source: [Node.js file system reference](https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html)
